title: Level 3 (Advanced) - C-19
notes:
West leads the ♥Q against 6♠. South is lucky to have avoided a club lead. South's club loser can be discarded on dummy's diamonds eventually. West's opening lead should be won in the dummy for a trump play.

When East follows low, South must decide what spade to play from hand. If the defensive spades are 2-2, playing a low spade from hand will be right when West has the ♠A and East has the ♠Q. If East has the ♠A and West has the ♠Q, it is necessary to play the ♠K. These two distributions are equally likely, making South's play a strict guess if spades are 2-2.

If West has a singleton ♠A, the contract will fail even if South plays a low spade from hand. West will win the ♠A and switch to clubs. South's best chance at this point is to play the ♠K, hoping for the ♠Q to drop.

South cannot, in practice, pick up 3 spades to the ♠A and ♠Q with East. If West has a singleton ♠Q, South can succeed by playing the ♠K from hand. As this is the only relevant 3-1 break, South should play the ♠K from his hand at trick 2.
